title: solidify
body:
## solidify

Gives a copy of the input surface a uniform shell thickness with Blender's Solidify modifier (Simple extrusion mode, rims on); offset places the shell inside, centred on or outside the original surface relative to its normals. Use it to turn sheets (plane, grid, wrapped or imported surfaces) into closed panels or shells that can be rendered with thickness, published as solid STL or used in boolean.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- thickness is in the input's local units; a scaled input yields a different world thickness.
- Inconsistent face normals make the shell grow in different directions; check normals of imported meshes.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `solidify`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `thickness` | Thickness of the generated shell. Negative values reverse the side towards which offset places it. | `{"type":"number"}` | `0.1` |
| `offset` | Where the shell lies relative to the original surface, measured along the face normals: -1 grows it entirely behind the surface (inwards for outward normals), 0 centres it and +1 grows it entirely in front. | `{"type":"number","minimum":-1,"maximum":1}` | `-1` |
